# dstqrb

> Computes all eigenvalues and the last components of the eigenvectors of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix using the implicit QL or QR method.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dstqrb from '@rreusser/blahpack/arpack/dstqrb';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dstqrb( N, d, strideD, e, strideE, Z, strideZ, WORK ) → INFO: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **in/out** · Subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · On exit, the last row of the orthonormal eigenvector matrix (length N) |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `Z` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N - 2</sub> | **out** · Workspace array (length >= 2\*(N-1)) |

**Returns** `INFO: integer`: 0 if successful, >0 if INFO eigenvalues did not converge

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` WORK array must have sufficient length

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dstqrb.ndarray(
    N,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    e, strideE, offsetE,
    Z, strideZ, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → INFO: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **in/out** · Subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| ↳ `offsetE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `e` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · On exit, the last row of the orthonormal eigenvector matrix (length N) |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `Z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `Z` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N - 2</sub> | **out** · Workspace array (length >= 2\*(N-1)) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

**Returns** `INFO: integer`: 0 if successful, >0 if INFO eigenvalues did not converge

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` WORK array must have sufficient length

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0` or `N === 1`.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dstqrb from '../base/lib/base.js';

// Symmetric tridiagonal matrix with diagonal 2 and subdiagonal -1:
const d = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0 ] );
const e = new Float64Array( [ -1.0, -1.0, -1.0 ] );
const Z = new Float64Array( 4 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 6 );

// Compute the eigenvalues and the last row of the eigenvector matrix:
const info = dstqrb( 4, d, 1, 0, e, 1, 0, Z, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );

console.log( info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 0

console.log( d ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => <Float64Array>[ ~0.382, ~1.382, ~2.618, ~3.618 ]

console.log( Z ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => last row of the orthonormal eigenvector matrix
```

</section>
